title_cn: 食品工业如何应对环孢子虫爆发

Since Taco Bell was linked to the cyclospora outbreak, the fast food chain removed the allegedly implicated lettuce from its supply chain and, in a bid to win back hesitant diners, began offering special discounts on a concoction known as the Enchirito.

Bloomberg Businessweek's Deena Shanker joins Max Chafkin and Stacey Vanek Smith on the Everybody's Business podcast to discuss how the food industry is dealing with the growing health crisis. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Rally as Soft Jobs Data Trims Fed Rate-Hike Bets
title_cn: 就业数据疲软削弱美联储加息押注，美国国债上涨
summary:
US Treasuries rallied after data showed employers unexpectedly cut jobs in July, suggesting labor market challenges that could impact the Federal Reserve’s willingness to raise interest rates.

The yield on two-year US Treasuries, which are sensitive to near-term moves in Fed monetary policy, fell as much as nine basis points on Friday to 4.15% as traders cut bets on interest-rate hikes in the coming months. The moves were pared later in the New York trading session as oil rose, though the two-year yield remained about four basis points lower on the day near 4.20%. We get reaction from Tom Tzitzouris, Head of Fixed Income Research at Baird Strategas. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cyclospora Outbreak Sends Shivers Through Restaurant Stocks
title_cn: 环孢菌爆发让餐馆股票不寒而栗
summary: The cyclospora outbreak in the U.S. tied to lettuce used in restaurants has made more than 10,000 people sick according to the Centers for Disease Control. This has caused fewer people to go out to eat or get fast food. Now this is starting to hurt the restaurant sector. R.J. Hottovy of Placer.ai research covers the space and joins "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Under Armour Cuts Sales View on Softer Demand Around the World

summary:
Under Armour Inc. forecast a sharper revenue decline than previously expected as demand softens in several key regions.
The athletic retailer now expects sales to fall by a mid-single digit percentage rate for the year. The revised forecast calls for declines in North America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe and the Middle East as the company grapples with a “challenging consumer demand environment,” Chief Executive Officer Kevin Plank said in a statement Friday. Bloomberg's Poonam Goyal joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. title: CAIS CEO Talks New Funding Round, AI’s Fintech Impact

summary: Matt Brown, Founder, Chairman, and CEO of CAIS, discussed the company's recent $170 million Series D funding round led by Vista and supported by AllianzBernstein, Blue Owl, and Carlyle, which values the alternative asset investment platform at over $2 billion—more than double its previous valuation. Brown highlighted CAIS's 37% organic growth and explained that the new capital will be used to pursue strategic mergers and acquisitions in response to ongoing fintech industry consolidation, enhance AI capabilities to improve the platform's user experience for advisers and asset managers, and provide liquidity to long-term shareholders through an institutional tender offer facilitated by Nasdaq Private Markets. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier discusses what Take-Two is calling “unprecedented” preorder demand, why expectations for the game are so high, and what to watch for when Rockstar unveils an extended look at GTA VI gameplay ahead of its November release. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: FCC Removes Nationwide Cap Limiting Local TV Ownership
title_cn: FCC 取消全国范围内限制本地电视所有权的上限
summary:
The Federal Communications Commission voted along party lines Thursday to repeal a nationwide audience cap that historically has limited the number of TV-viewing households a single broadcaster could reach. 
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr led the vote overturning two decades of precedent in favor of a new case-by-case approach and teeing up a legal issue that is almost certainly headed for federal appeals court. Bloomberg's Matthew Schettenhelm joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NEC's Hassett on US Job Losses, Fed Independence, Iran, Energy Prices
title_cn: NEC 哈塞特谈美国失业、美联储独立、伊朗、能源价格
summary: White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett says he's focused on the breakeven hiring rate in the July jobs report. Hassett also says President Donald Trump does talk to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh about the economy all the time, but Trump respects the Fed's independence. Hassett speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Spain and Italy Step Up Border Control Fight Over Migrant Crisis
title_cn: 西班牙和意大利加强边境管制应对移民危机
summary: Spain and Italy’s feud over migration escalated after Rome bluntly refused to lift new border controls imposed after the sudden influx of 70,000 migrants to a Spanish African enclave.

title: Nationalizing Water Would Cost £140 Billion, Burnham Is Told
title_cn: 伯纳姆获悉，水务国有化将耗资 1400 亿英镑
summary: Creditors of Thames Water have told the UK government it would cost £40 billion ($53.8 billion) more than previously thought to nationalize England’s water companies, in a bid to stop Prime Minister Andy Burnham taking extreme steps to give the public more control over the industry.
